quotes.text: Unstructured data is anything that doesn't fit neatly into rows and columns. A photo of your dog, a product demo video, a web server, log file, a database backup, a PDF contract.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A tangible definition of the data Blob Storage is built for.

quotes.text: If it's a file someone uploads or downloads, use a block blob. If it's a continuous stream of log entries or sensor readings, use an append blob. If it's a virtual machine disk, use a page blob
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A simple rule for choosing between the three blob types.

quotes.text: Moving data between tiers cost money. Every time you change a blob's tier, you pay a transaction fee. If you shuffle things around every few days, those fees eat up any savings you thought you were getting.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns about a hidden cost trap of access tiers.

quotes.text: Pick the right tier for your access pattern and leave it there. Don't try to game the system by moving things constantly.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear, actionable recommendation on access tiers.

quotes.text: And remember redundancy protects your data, not your application. You still need to design your application to handle failures gracefully.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies a common misconception about what storage redundancy covers.

chapters.title: Intro: what Blob Storage is for
Hot, cool, cold and archive tiers

takeaways: Blob Storage is flat object storage for unstructured data, organized as storage account, container and blob.
Block, append and page blobs serve files, logs and VM disks, while hot, cool, cold and archive tiers trade storage cost against access cost, automated by lifecycle management rules.
Prefer Microsoft Entra ID with Azure RBAC over account keys and SAS tokens, and choose LRS, ZRS or GZRS based on how critical the data is.
hook: Azure Blob Storage is probably the cloud storage service you use most without knowing it. This episode explains the account-container-blob hierarchy, blob types, access tiers, lifecycle rules, security and redundancy for Azure beginners, so they can store unstructured data safely and cheaply.
